Dear Ivy SEAH

Thank you for your prompt review of our proposal.

We are continuing to review the FEM model on our side as well, and it has been confirmed that the stress on the lower part of the stringer remains within the allowable stress range.

However, due to the 150mm gap between the proposed 120x10 FACE plate and the shell plate, it is not feasible to carry out welding work. Therefore, we would like to propose using a 75x15 doubler plate instead of the 120x10 FACE plate.

The 75mm width of the FACE bar is the maximum allowable width for welding work. We kindly ask for your review and approval of this alternative.

Best regards,

Dear Mr. Choi,

Good day.  
We have no objection to your proposal on adding a doubler plate to strengthen the existing face plate.  
However, a doubler plate of at least 120x10mm shall be fitted using slot weld, and fillet weld is used to connect the doubler plate behind.

Slot weld shall comply to the requirements in NR561, Sec 3, 2.4.  
The doubler plate shall extend to the stringer face plate.  
The face plate below the stringer shall be fitted with doubler plate as well.

This modification is applicable to Side Frame Fr.5, Fr. 7, Fr.9 and Fr.11.  
Kindly refer below sketch.  
Please get owner's agreement on this modification.

Dear **Ivy SEAH**

With regard to the soft patch opening, we have conducted an on-site inspection of the vessel in order to reflect your comments.

However, we have received feedback from the shipyard indicating that, due to interferences with various equipment, piping, and electrical cables,

it is not possible to install the removable box member.

Furthermore, at this stage, it is also not possible to remove the 75x10 face and install a new 100x15 FACE by welding it to the 150x8 WEB member.

Accordingly, we would like to propose the following alternative, which avoids such interferences and allows for possible welding work.  
The proposed method is outlined below for your review, and we kindly request your feedback after review.

Should you have any questions or require additional information, please do not hesitate to contact us.

Thank you and best regards,

-BELOW

Dear Mr. Choi,

Good day.  
We have performed another independent assessment with finite element model, the conclusion remained the same as we previously presented via our beam model.

The side frame stress has exceeded the rule criteria.  
Designer/yard to consider further reinforcement for the side frame Fr.5, Fr. 7, Fr.9 and Fr.11, i.e, increase of face plate scantling to at least FB100x15.  
Alternatively, a removable box section can be installed to reinforce the side shell (refer figure below).  
This box section shall always be present during the voyage and only be removed in dry dock for maintenance purposes.  
Do let us know if you have any clarifications.  
We can schedule a meeting and discuss in teams.

 ![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Best Regards,

Dear Mr. Choi,

Good day.

Please find below our comments to be considered.

1. Model extension – model to be extended to cover complete engine room from Fr.1.5 to Fr.15.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

2. Boundary conditions – please specify the boundary conditions considered. The boundaries are to be applied at bulkhead Fr.1.5 and Fr.15 only.
3. Sea Pressure – pressure to be applied in linear based on the elevation z.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

4. Based on NR396, Ch3, C3.7.8.3 and C3.7.9.3 the allowable stress limit are 70/k and 70/k-σ respectively. It is advisable to include the deck loading of 8.24kN/m2 in the analysis. With this, the allowable stress limit is 70/k=70/0.8=87.5MPa.
5. Mesh size to be provided.

Best Regards,
